newsitem.title: USA: Former Mercury chairman's estate sells shares.
newsitem.headline: Former Mercury chairman's estate sells shares.

text.p: The estate of Daniel Terra, former chairman of Mercury Finance Co, sold 1.9 million shares of the company's stock in February, shortly after the beleaguered automobile finance company's stock plummeted, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The shares were sold between February 11 and February 26 at prices ranging from $2 a share to $3.725, the filing said.
The shares, sold by executor James Terra, Daniel Terra's son, were sold to raise cash to pay the estate's general obligations, the filing said.
After the sale, Terra held 14.9 million or about 8.4 percent of Mercury's shares outstanding as of November 1996.
Terra expects to sell 500,000 additional shares by March 12, according to the filing.
In late January, Mercury said it would have to lower its earnings over the last four years by about $90 million, due to accounting discrepancies.
The stock plunged from the $14 range to below $2 after the news.
Mercury shares were unchanged at $3.25 Thursday.
